title: Hamming-ball bound for function spaces
statement:
Let $\alpha$ and $\beta$ be finite types, fix a function $\mathrm{center} : \alpha \to \beta$, and let $e \in \bbn$. Then the number of functions $f : \alpha \to \beta$ that disagree with $\mathrm{center}$ on at most $e$ points of $\alpha$ — that is, for which $\abs{\{a \in \alpha : \mathrm{center}(a) \ne f(a)\}} \le e$ — satisfies
\[
\abs{\{\, f : \alpha \to \beta \;:\; \abs{\{a \in \alpha : \mathrm{center}(a) \ne f(a)\}} \le e \,\}} \;\le\; \sum_{t=0}^{e} \binom{\abs{\alpha}}{t}\,\abs{\beta}^{\,t}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: center is a fixed function α → β
replaced:
For finite types $\alpha, \beta$, a center function $\mathrm{center} : \alpha \to \beta$
and a radius $e$, the number of functions $f : \alpha \to \beta$ that differ from the
center on at most $e$ coordinates is bounded by
\[
\sum_{t=0}^{e} \binom{\abs{\alpha}}{t}\,\abs{\beta}^{\,t}.
\]
This is a slightly coarser form of the usual bound, which carries
$(\abs{\beta}-1)^t$ in place of $\abs{\beta}^t$.
